newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Petron to cut workforce by 25 pct. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Petron to cut workforce by 25 pct. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]

text.p: Philippine oil refiner Petron Corp is reducing its 1,700 workforce by 25 percent over a six-month period from January, president Ali Al-Ajmi said on Thursday. (Corrects size of workforce from 17,000)
"We are reducing the manpower to attain a leaner organisation. We are undergoing major reorganisation to improve key business processes," he told analysts.
Al-Ajmi did not say what financial impact the reduction of the workforce would have on the company.

Petron vice-president Motassim Al-Maashouq said that although the company suffered losses as a result of an automatic oil price adjustment formula, the oil firms expect better performance by full deregulation in March 1997.
The formula introduced in August allowed adjustments in monthly oil prices but instead of using crude oil prices as benchmark it made use of Singapore Posted Prices (SPP) as the basis.
"But with the onset of full deregulation, sound business fundamentals will reflect itself," the Petron official said.
Al-Maashouq said petroleum demand is expected to grow by 6.4 percent annually from 1996 to 2005 with liquefied petroleum gasoline posting the highest growth rate.
He said Petron awaits for the settlement of its 1.2 billion pesos in claims from the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF), an oil buffer fund.
